groups.label: Directions (Q1-Q5)
groups.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:

Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight line, all facing north. All of them sit at an equal distance from one another.

questions.question: Who sits at the extreme right end of the row?
questions.solution:
Arrangement (left to right): R - S - U - Q - P - T

Let us place them one by one:
1. P sits second to the right of U → if U is at position 3, P is at position 5.
2. R sits second to the left of U → R is at position 1.
3. S sits third to the left of P → P is at 5, so S is at position 2.
4. T sits at an extreme end and P already occupies the right end (6) → T is at position 6.
5. Q sits between T and R → the only free seat between them is position 4, so Q is at 4.

Final order: R, S, U, Q, P, T. Hence the extreme right end is occupied by T.

questions.question: Who sits second to the left of Q?
questions.solution:
Final arrangement: R(1) - S(2) - U(3) - Q(4) - P(5) - T(6).

Q is at position 4. Two places to its left is position 2, which is occupied by S.

questions.question: How many persons sit between U and T?
questions.solution:
Final arrangement: R - S - U - Q - P - T.

U is at position 3 and T is at position 6. The persons strictly between them are Q (4) and P (5) → 2 persons.

questions.question: Who sits immediately to the right of S?
questions.solution:
Final arrangement: R - S - U - Q - P - T.

S is at position 2. The seat immediately to its right (position 3) is occupied by U.

questions.question: What is the position of P with respect to R?
questions.solution:
Final arrangement: R(1) - S(2) - U(3) - Q(4) - P(5) - T(6).

R is at position 1 and P is at position 5. Counting from R towards the right: S, U, Q, P → P is the 4th person to the right of R.

questions.question:
Statements:
All pens are books.
Some books are pencils.

Conclusions:
I. Some pens are pencils.
II. Some pencils are books.
questions.solution:
Conclusion I - 'Some pens are pencils': We know all pens are books, and some books are pencils. The 'some books' that are pencils may or may not include pens. So this does not definitely follow.

Conclusion II - 'Some pencils are books': 'Some books are pencils' is a particular affirmative statement, and 'some' is reversible. So 'some pencils are books' definitely follows.

Hence only II follows.

questions.question:
Statements:
P > Q ≥ R = S < T

Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. T > R
questions.solution:
Conclusion I - P > S: From the statement, P > Q ≥ R = S. Since P > Q and Q ≥ S, we get P > S. This follows.

Conclusion II - T > R: From R = S < T, we have T > S and S = R, so T > R. This follows.

Both conclusions follow.

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl in the photograph related to the man?
questions.solution:
Work backwards through the relations:

• My grandfather's only son = the man's father (since the grandfather has only one son).
• Daughter of my father = the man's sister (or the man himself, but the person is referred to as 'she').

So the girl is the man's sister.
